title: Manure Evaluation and Vaginal Discharge
text:
What to look at?
- Consistency and texture
- Odor
- Color
- Presence of parasite eggs.

Factors that may affect the cow's manure?
- Weather condition
- Sudden change in the diet
- Nutritional deficiency
- Hydration status
- Disease and infection
- Parasitism
- Fresh cows

3. VAGINAL DISCHARGE

What to look at?
- Color
- Odor
- Consistency

facts: When evaluating a cow's manure, key characteristics to look at include consistency and texture, odor, color, and presence of parasite eggs.
Factors that can affect cow's manure include weather condition, sudden change in diet, nutritional deficiency, hydration status, disease and infection, parasitism, and being a fresh cow.
Section 3 covers vaginal discharge in dairy cows.
When evaluating vaginal discharge, the characteristics to look at are color, odor, and consistency.
Vaginal discharge in cows in heat appears clear and stringy/mucous.
Post-calving vaginal discharge is monitored specifically 3-5 days post calving.

What three properties should be examined when evaluating a cow's vaginal discharge?

options.C: Viscosity, glucose level, and parasite count

questions.question: According to the photograph labels on post-calving monitoring, within what timeframe is the post-calving discharge highlighted?
Based on the image labeled 'Cows in heat', what visual characteristic is typical of vaginal discharge during estrus?

options.A: Clear, stringy mucous discharge hanging from the vulva

questions.question: Which statement regarding factors affecting cow manure is TRUE according to the text?

options.A: Hydration status and parasitism are both factors that may affect a cow's manure.
options.B: Weather conditions have no effect on a cow's manure consistency.
options.C: Fresh cows produce manure that is completely unaffected by physiological changes.
options.D: Nutritional deficiencies only alter urine, never manure.
